title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment (study id cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that tested whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces verifier‑detected semantic/safety failures for intent→vendor‑CLI NetOps tasks. Planned N=300 intent pairs; after preregistered exclusions 266 complete pairs were analysed. Baseline initial-candidate passes = 260/266 (97.744%); final guarded (GVR) passes = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.018797; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037594, 0.03759398]. We executed the preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats excluded/failed episodes as failures (complete N=300): baseline 260/300 (86.667%), guarded 265/300 (88.333%), paired difference = 0.016667; exact McNemar p = 0.0625; approximate 95% CI (paired normal approximation using archived discordant counts) = [0.00220, 0.03114]. Repair was invoked rarely (6 recorded repair calls). Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule the observed improvement does not reach confirmatory significance; inference is sensitive to the very small number of discordant pairs (n10=5, n01=0). We present the preregistered design, deterministic validation rule, recorded runtime model settings and artifact pointers, the confirmatory and sensitivity numeric results, and an evidence‑grounded discussion of operational implications and validity threats. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the paper.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation and zero‑touch configuration generation [1,2]. Stochastic LLM outputs can produce syntactic or semantic violations that lead to unsafe network states; therefore pipelines that interpose deterministic validators and bounded repair loops (generate–verify–repair, GVR) are proposed to improve operational trustworthiness [3]. We evaluate, under a preregistered paired design (shared_initial_candidate semantics), whether a GVR pipeline—one LLM initial candidate per task (gpt‑5‑mini), deterministic Batfish‑style verification (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and at most one automated LLM repair—reduces verifier‑detected failures relative to the same initial candidate when no repair is invoked. Our principal contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived confirmatory test of the validator‑triggered repair effect on a deterministic task corpus and an evidence‑grounded sensitivity analysis that treats excluded episodes as failures.
sections.related_work: Prior work describes intent‑to‑CLI translation prototypes and benchmarks for LLMs in NetOps and proposes GVR‑style architectures and verifier integration to reduce hallucinations and semantic errors [4,5,6]. Surveys emphasise grounding approaches (RAG, tool augmentation) and document LLM failure modes that motivate deterministic validators [2,7]. Network‑verification tools (Batfish and header‑space analyses) have been proposed as deterministic oracles for automated pipelines [5]. Our study differs by executing a preregistered paired experiment with archived raw outputs, deterministic validator traces, and a planned sensitivity analysis derived from the same artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The completed preregistration (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1; preregistration SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891) fixed a paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, and N=300 intent pairs (150 Cisco‑like, 150 Juniper‑like) drawn from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a deterministic synthetic generator. Execution contract mandated exactly one initial model generation per task and at most one automated repair call when the deterministic validator failed. Deterministic validation: the archived validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performs syntactic parsing, required‑sequence and reachability checks, and emits pass/fail plus violation codes; the binary pass/fail outcome is the primary endpoint. Recorded model configuration: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd) declares declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens = 1024, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null. The recorded temperature value is null (unset) and no explicit deterministic sampling seed is present in the archived configuration; therefore nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded and is disclosed. Execution accounting and missingness: planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68; complete paired units after exclusions = 266 (missingness_summary.csv archived). Retry policy and exclusion rules followed the preregistration (up to 2 automatic retries for transient provider failures; irrecoverable failures excluded per 'complete_pair_primary'). Sensitivity analysis: per the preregistration we executed the 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' analysis using the archived episode accounting: failed both‑arm pairs (34) were treated as double‑failures (added to n00) to produce a conservative paired table on the full planned N=300. Analysis methods: primary confirmatory test = exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes; paired difference CIs reported via paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the main 266‑pair analysis and via an approximate paired normal formula (derived from archived discordant counts) for the sensitivity N=300 analysis. All raw model outputs, validator traces, provider call logs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived (execution manifest paths and hashes referenced in the evidence bundle).
sections.results: Primary (preregistered) analysis — complete pairs = 266: baseline successes = 260/266 (0.9774436090); guarded final successes = 265/266 (0.9962406015). Paired contingency (guarded,baseline): n11=260, n10=5, n01=0, n00=1. Paired difference = (265−260)/266 = 0.01879699248. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered primary decision α=0.05 → not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729, archived bootstrap procedure) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair activity: provider_call_audit(stage_counts) records shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6 (six repair calls executed). Missingness: 34 episodes were excluded as both‑arm infrastructure/model failures per the preregistered plan; missingness_summary.csv archived. Sensitivity analysis (preregistered, now executed using archived accounting) — treat failed episodes as failures: N = planned 300 pairs with concordant extra failures: n11=260, n10=5, n01=0, n00=35 (added 34 both‑missing pairs to n00). Baseline successes = 260/300 = 0.8666666667; guarded successes = 265/300 = 0.8833333333; paired difference = 5/300 = 0.0166666667. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (discordant counts unchanged). Approximate 95% CI (paired normal approximation using archived discordant counts and standard paired‑difference variance formula applied to N=300) = [0.00220, 0.03114]. Interpretation: both the main complete‑pair bootstrap CI and the sensitivity CI lie (narrowly) above zero, but the exact McNemar two‑sided p (the preregistered decision rule) remains 0.0625 because the inferential test depends only on discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0). The small number of discordant pairs limits confirmatory power despite a positive point estimate.
sections.discussion: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (≈1.9 percentage points on complete pairs; ≈1.67 percentage points on full planned N) in verifier pass rate. Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar decision rule the result does not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The discrepancy between the two‑sided exact test and the resampling CI arises because the exact test is discrete and depends only on discordant counts; with very few discordants a two‑sided exact p can exceed 0.05 even when a resampling CI excludes zero. Operationally, the low repair invocation rate (6 repairs out of 300 initial generations) indicates that for this model/task corpus the initial candidates were already highly likely to satisfy the deterministic validator, leaving limited headroom for guarded repair to improve outcomes. Implications: deterministic validators integrated into LLM pipelines can provide deterministic pass/fail assurance and enable bounded automated repair, but marginal benefit depends on baseline failure rate, validator coverage, vendor dialect complexity, and repair‑convertibility of errors. Limitations of inference (small discordant counts), sampling nondeterminism (temperature unset in the archived model configuration), and the restricted task corpus constrain generalisability; broader evaluations across vendor dialects, higher baseline failure regimes, and differing generation strategies are needed.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment evaluating a GVR pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks. Across 266 completed pairs the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate by 0.01880 (1.88 percentage points) but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 threshold (p=0.0625). The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating failed episodes as failures (N=300) yields a paired difference = 0.01667 and p = 0.0625 with an approximate 95% CI = [0.00220, 0.03114]. Repair calls were rare (6), limiting potential guarded benefit for this corpus and model. We archive all execution and analysis artifacts to support further exploration; future work should evaluate workloads with higher baseline failure rates, expanded validator coverage, alternative constrained‑generation strategies, and human‑in‑the‑loop escalation studies.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy and artifacts: The study was executed autonomously after an explicit autonomy lock. Models/tools: recorded model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, sha256: 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd), orchestration adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: before the autonomy lock a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; after the lock no human edited or rewrote technical content, prompts, outputs, analyses, or manuscript text. Reproducibility: execution and analysis artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/results.json, task_manifest.jsonl, model_configuration.json, paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, analysis logs) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle; representative artifact hashes are included in the archived manifest. Nondeterminism disclosure: the archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no explicit deterministic sampling seed; therefore nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for the recorded model calls.
limitations: Sample and missingness: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/API exclusions 266 pairs completed and 34 episodes were lost and excluded per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule—this reduces effective sample size and precision.

Sensitivity analysis: the preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats failed episodes/pairs as failures (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity) has been executed using archived episode accounting; numeric results are reported in Results. The preregistered alternative sensitivity of treating flagged contamination items differently remains exploratory if pursued.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation per the preregistration; measured effect is strictly the validator‑triggered repair benefit and does not evaluate independent constrained‑prompt generations or alternative first‑pass strategies.

Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provides a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability checks; semantic violations outside the validator's coverage are possible and unmeasured.
Small discordant counts: primary inference relied on exact McNemar with very few discordant pairs (n10=5, n01=0); interpretive conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.

Runtime sampling settings: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no deterministic seed; null does not imply deterministic sampling and nondeterminism cannot be excluded from the archive.

External validity: tasks were drawn from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a deterministic synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal GVR benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production environments.
